questions.prompt: A \(0.25\,\mathrm{kg}\) ball moves at \(16\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find its momentum magnitude.
A constant \(12\,\mathrm{N}\) force acts for \(0.50\,\mathrm{s}\). Find the impulse magnitude.
A \(0.15\,\mathrm{kg}\) ball moves right at \(10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), then rebounds left at \(6.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the impulse on the ball, taking right as positive.
questions.answer:
Take right as positive:
\[
J=m(v_f-v_i)=0.15(-6.0-10)=-2.4\,\mathrm{N\,s}
\]
The impulse is \(2.4\,\mathrm{N\,s}\) left.

questions.prompt: A \(0.060\,\mathrm{kg}\) ball moving at \(30\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) is stopped in \(0.010\,\mathrm{s}\). Find the average force on the ball.
questions.answer:
Take the initial motion as positive:
\[
J=m(0-30)=-1.8\,\mathrm{N\,s}
\]
\[
F_{\mathrm{avg}}=\frac{J}{\Delta t}=\frac{-1.8}{0.010}=-180\,\mathrm{N}
\]
The force is opposite the initial motion.

questions.prompt: A force-time graph is triangular with height \(80\,\mathrm{N}\) and base \(0.20\,\mathrm{s}\). The impulse acts on a \(2.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) object initially at rest. Find its final speed.
questions.answer:
The impulse is the triangle area:
\[
J=\frac{1}{2}(0.20)(80)=8.0\,\mathrm{N\,s}
\]
Starting from rest,
\[
\Delta v=\frac{J}{m}=\frac{8.0}{2.0}=4.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: A \(3.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) object initially at rest receives impulse \(\vec{J}=6\hat{\imath}-2\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{N\,s}\). Find its final velocity vector.
A force of \(30\,\mathrm{N}\) acts for \(0.20\,\mathrm{s}\), then \(10\,\mathrm{N}\) acts in the opposite direction for \(0.30\,\mathrm{s}\). Find the net impulse.
questions.answer:
Take the first force direction as positive:
\[
J=30(0.20)-10(0.30)=6.0-3.0=3.0\,\mathrm{N\,s}
\]
The net impulse is in the first force direction.

questions.prompt: Two safety pads bring the same runner to rest. Pad A stops the runner in \(0.10\,\mathrm{s}\); pad B stops the runner in \(0.40\,\mathrm{s}\). Compare the average stopping forces and interpret the result.
questions.answer:
Both pads produce the same momentum change:
\[
F_{\mathrm{avg}}\Delta t=\Delta p
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac{F_B}{F_A}=\frac{0.10}{0.40}=\frac{1}{4}
\]
Pad B gives one quarter of the average stopping force because it spreads the same impulse over four times longer.

questions.prompt: A \(0.50\,\mathrm{kg}\) puck hits a wall and rebounds with half its incoming speed. The contact lasts \(0.020\,\mathrm{s}\), and the average force magnitude from the wall is \(90\,\mathrm{N}\). Find the incoming speed. State the sign convention and the modeling assumption.
questions.answer:
Take the incoming direction as positive. Then
\[
v_i=u,\qquad v_f=-\frac{u}{2}
\]
The impulse magnitude is
\[
J=F_{\mathrm{avg}}\Delta t=90(0.020)=1.8\,\mathrm{N\,s}
\]
and
\[
|J|=m\left|-\frac{u}{2}-u\right|=\frac{3}{2}mu
\]
So
\[
u=\frac{1.8}{(3/2)(0.50)}=2.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
Assumption: the wall's average force accounts for the contact impulse and other impulses during contact are negligible. The impulse is opposite the incoming motion.

questions.prompt: A mass \(m\) moves in the positive \(x\)-direction with speed \(u\). During \(0<t<\tau\), a force pulse acts in the negative \(x\)-direction with magnitude \(F(t)=F_0(1-t/\tau)\). Derive the condition on \(F_0\tau\) for the mass to leave with speed at least \(\beta u\) in the negative \(x\)-direction. State assumptions.
questions.answer:
Assume one-dimensional motion, constant mass, and no other impulse. The force is negative, so
\[
J_x=-\int_0^\tau F_0\left(1-\frac{t}{\tau}\right)dt=-\frac{F_0\tau}{2}
\]
The final velocity is
\[
v_f=u+\frac{J_x}{m}=u-\frac{F_0\tau}{2m}
\]
To leave with speed at least \(\beta u\) in the negative direction,
\[
v_f\le -\beta u
\]
so
\[
F_0\tau\ge 2m(1+\beta)u
\]
Interpretation: the pulse area must remove the original momentum and add the required reverse momentum.
